attempts.prompt:
Korean webtoon panel, digitally inked and coloured by a professional webtoon studio. Crisp black ink with tapered strokes, heavier on the outer silhouette, the jaw, the hair mass and where forms overlap. Flat local colour with one hard-edged cool cel shadow per material. One named key light: its colour washes smoothly over the lit side. If the scene names a back light, it draws a thin crisp rim along the figure's silhouette. Everything else stays flat. Muted cool base palette of slate, navy and grey-blue, so the light source and the character's signature colour carry the saturation. Background simplified and lower in contrast than the characters. Small crisp highlights; glossy specular only on metal and wet surfaces.
Hand-made webtoon colouring: each garment has only a few large, opaque, clean-edged shadow shapes, placed in its real folds; no scattered translucent streaks, zigzag shards or crumpled-foil folds. Worn cloth shows a few small frayed notches and loose threads, never sawtooth edges along every edge. Plain shoes and clothes with no logos, stripes or brand marks. Every strap, buckle, pocket and seam is attached and has a purpose; no stray stitch marks. Matte skin, hair and stone; no 3D, low-poly or plastic look.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: a fully detailed exterior location key, one single landscape image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, PNG.
Recipe: establish. Street-level camera height 1.6 m on the opposite pavement, a broad view across a normal Mapo street in Seoul, looking slightly up at one unfinished concrete tower. Show the entire building from pavement to exposed roof rebar with sky above, without cropping. Near-frontal three-quarter view with the facade easy to count and coherent perspective. Orange dusk sky is the visible key light; dusty warm orange light on concrete edges, broad cool slate/violet cel shadows inside the floors. Keep the drawing and colours consistent with reference 1.

Reference images: image 1 (tower_gate/key.png) is ONLY the approved tower's concrete column-and-beam construction, green safety mesh, dusty orange dusk lighting and V2 rendering reference. Draw the OUTSIDE, not that interior view. Image 2 (sewer_gate/outside.png) is ONLY the gate's narrow irregular vertical tear shape, black-violet core and thin pale rim reference; do not copy its location or its night lighting.

The main subject is ONE unfinished TWELVE-STOREY concrete building. It has twelve distinct open habitable storey spaces, all bare concrete columns and slabs, without exterior walls or glass. Make all twelve rows of openings clearly visible, uniformly spaced, so the reader can count them. Count upward from the street: the open ground storey is storey ONE; above it are TWO, THREE, FOUR, FIVE, SIX, SEVEN, EIGHT, NINE, TEN, ELEVEN, TWELVE. A flat roof slab caps the twelfth storey, and exposed upright rebar rises above that roof. No extra penthouse, podium storey, mezzanine or additional partial storey. Do not put numbers or labels into the picture. Keep a clear uncovered front bay spanning the whole height for counting. The building is about 36 m tall, with each storey about 3 m high; pedestrians about 1.7 m, street light poles about 8 m.

On the SEVENTH open storey counted from ground = 1, place a single narrow jagged VERTICAL SLIT of black-violet light, with a hairline pale white-cyan rim. Six complete open storeys below its storey and five complete open storeys above its storey. Its pointed, uneven outline bends slightly like a tear in space, exactly as the slit in reference 2. It is roughly 2.1 m tall and only about 0.25 m wide, very narrow in the wide shot; the base meets the seventh-floor slab, and the top stops clearly below the beam overhead. It is a freestanding spatial tear in the open concrete bay: NO frame, NO lintel, NO rectangular portal or doorway. A tiny pale violet spill touches only the adjacent concrete. All other bays are empty.

Scaffolding climbs ONE side of the tower, covered partly with green safety mesh, with a few loose mesh edges and translucent plastic sheets visibly flapping in the breeze. Keep this to a narrow side strip so it does not hide the countable floors. A low blank site hoarding runs along the far pavement at the building's base, below the top of the ground-storey openings. Low ordinary neighbourhood buildings on either side, understated utility wires and ordinary street lights turning on, blank shop signs, an orange dusk sky. One or two tiny anonymous adult pedestrians on the far pavement in front of the hoarding, full adult proportions, feet on the same pavement plane, for correct scale. Normal dry asphalt street in foreground. Full location detail with restrained clean cel shading and crisp structural lines, no painterly or photographic texture.

No text, letters, numbers, speech bubbles, captions, sound-effect lettering, interface windows or readable signs. Emblems without letters are fine; no brand logos or wordmarks. Not a 3D render, not a photograph, no photographic background. No airbrushed skin, no plastic gloss on skin or hair, no haze or bloom over the whole image, no depth-of-field blur, no lens flare unless a real camera flash is in the scene. No watermark or signature. Correct hands with five fingers. No chibi proportions unless the brief says chibi. No compressed or stubby bodies, no shortened legs or torsos, no oversized heads; no people out of scale with the doors, vehicles and buildings around them; no figures floating off the floor or breaking the scene's perspective.
attempts.review: Too few open storeys (nine clearly visible bands); slit too tall for the storey, reaching across a beam; pedestrians oversized against storey height.

EXACT FLOOR COUNT: twelve storeys = SIX LOWER STOREYS + SIX UPPER STOREYS. Do not accidentally draw eleven.
LOWER HALF: six clearly distinct storeys between pavement and the middle slab. First is the open street-level ground storey; second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth above it. All six must be visible and countable.
UPPER HALF: six more clearly distinct storeys between the middle slab and the flat roof. The first upper storey is number seven and holds the slit; above that are eight, nine, ten, eleven and twelve. All six upper storeys must be visible and countable.
There are THIRTEEN slab planes bounding the TWELVE open horizontal storey spaces. Count them before finishing. The open bands must all have the same 3 m storey height. Make the tower narrow enough and each band shallow enough that all twelve fit. No roof room or extra storey.

The gate is in the LOWEST storey of the UPPER SIX: exactly the seventh floor. SIX COMPLETE STOREYS BELOW ITS FLOOR, FIVE COMPLETE STOREYS ABOVE ITS CEILING. Its base touches the seventh-floor slab and its top is below the ceiling. Never a rectangle, framed door or arch. No solid wall behind it.

Exposed rebar on top. Side scaffolding with green safety mesh and loose plastic sheeting flapping. All twelve rows on the front facade stay visible. The construction hoarding is LOW in the drawing and only hides the bottom quarter of the street-level storey, so all ground-floor pillars and the open ground-floor space above it are readable. No tall trees or neighbouring objects covering the front tower.
Ordinary low neighbourhood buildings, ordinary street lights and a dry road surrounding the tower. One or two VERY TINY pedestrians on the far pavement for scale, each less than half a storey high at that distance, about one twentieth of tower height, full adult proportions. Keep them small.
